newsitem.title: LEBANON: Israeli forces seize Lebanese journalist.
newsitem.headline: Israeli forces seize Lebanese journalist.

text.p: Israeli forces have seized a Lebanese television journalist and a businessman in south Lebanon and taken them to Israel, a pro-Israeli militia source said on Thursday.

The source said Roger Nahra, a cameraman for Lebanon's MTV private television network, was taken by the Israeli forces from his house early on Thursday in the village of Qlaiaa in Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone.
The Israelis also seized a businessman identified as Jean Nahra, a relative of the cameraman, the source said.
"Israeli forces entered the village and took Nahra (the cameraman) from his house to Israel," said the source.
Nahra is based in Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone as cameraman for MTV. Roger Matar, MTV news operations manager in Beirut, confirmed his seizure.
"He was arrested at around 1:00 in the morning. We are making contacts to try and win his release," he said.
Gabriel al-Murr, the brother of Lebanese Interior Minister Michel al-Murr, is a major shareholder in MTV.
Hizbollah (Party of God) guerrillas are fighting to oust Israeli troops and their local militia allies from a 15-km (nine miles)-wide border zone they hold in south Lebanon.

Israel has held a border strip uninterruptedly since its first invasion of Lebanon in 1978. It set the current boundaries of the zone in 1985 after withdrawing the bulk of its forces following a second invasion in 1982.
